scope: Provisional crosswalk for user-owned plugin/harness; comparison only, no catalogue modifications.
source_contract: docs/writing-harness/paragraph-functions.json version 0.1 and accepted-foundations.md. Twelve functions may coexist; do not infer mandatory one-label paragraphs.

mapping_kinds.conditional: possible only when listed conditions hold
mapping_kinds.partial: overlap with some uses, not equivalent
mapping_kinds.relation_only: source encodes a relation; function mapping requires contextual projection
mapping_kinds.none: no determinate mapping from label alone

technical_observations: Webis archive TXT actual split-by-portal-final: 300 files; row counts include continued 25933, no-unit 16399, assumption 9805, par-sep 4664, anecdote 2607, testimony 1091, statistics 421, title 300, common-ground 243, other 167. These are row counts, not final-unit counts.
Webis paper reports final 14313 units; its six categories are forced single labels, with segmentation and post-processing, and gives no claim target graph.
Argument microtext DTD distinguishes edu, adu, joint, ADU role pro/opp, document stance pro/con/unclear, and six edges. Undercut targets an edge; source taxonomy must not be flattened.
Source-published output supports mechanical integrity and provenance checks; semantic relevance, adequacy and paragraph function still require human editorial review.

records.unit: argumentative discourse unit; proposition span of at most one sentence
records.definition: General issues represented as accepted without proof by nearly all possible readers.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Orientation requires contextual preparation for the next contribution; a supposedly shared general claim can instead be part of the argument. Shared acceptance is annotator judgment, not verified truth.
records.computable_validation: Check label vocabulary and paragraph membership; context and audience acceptance require review.

records.unit: argumentative discourse unit; proposition span of at most one sentence
records.definition: Author assumption, conclusion, judgment, opinion, general observation or potentially false fact requiring support.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: A genuine position can be assert, observation report, and conclusion interpret only when it develops an inference; not every declarative proposition is assert.
records.computable_validation: Check span boundaries and paragraph overlap; assertion ownership and interpretation need review.

records.unit: argumentative discourse unit; proposition span of at most one sentence
records.definition: Evidence via an attributed proposition from an expert, authority, witness, organization or similar.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Report if it faithfully attributes what was said. Support requires a recoverable claim and a connection; attribution alone does not prove truth or support.
records.computable_validation: Check attribution and recorded target references when present; Webis lacks argument-target links, so semantic support needs new annotation.

records.unit: argumentative discourse unit; proposition span of at most one sentence
records.definition: Quantitative research, empirical analysis results or conclusions presented as evidence, with optional reference.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: A numeric result can be reported; support requires an identified claim and meaningful connection. A figure by itself is not support, and a reference is not proof.
records.computable_validation: Validate numeric/text span, paragraph and optional target IDs; determine evidential connection by review.

records.unit: argumentative discourse unit; proposition span of at most one sentence
records.definition: Personal experience, anecdote, concrete instance, example or specific event given as evidence.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Specific event alone is not narrative: narrate needs experience developed through time/change. Illustrate needs an idea illuminated; support needs identifiable claim and connection.
records.computable_validation: Check spans, instance and paragraph alignment; event development, illustrative purpose and claim connection need review.

records.unit: argumentative discourse unit; proposition span of at most one sentence
records.definition: Adds little or nothing to argumentative discourse, or does not match prior five categories.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Unmatched in this argument scheme does not mean no function in the harness; no individual target function can be inferred.
records.computable_validation: Preserve exact source label and route to open review; never reject or auto-label a paragraph from this value.

records.definition: Segment outside an argumentative unit, including punctuation in final post-processing.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Structural processing marker; neither a negative example nor a paragraph-function class. Preserve punctuation and original markers.
records.computable_validation: Validate row types and count, continuation chains and paragraph separators; retain optional fourth field and original sequence.

records.definition: Segment merged with subsequent segments until terminal unit class.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Structural processing marker; neither a negative example nor a paragraph-function class. Preserve punctuation and original markers.
records.computable_validation: Validate row types and count, continuation chains and paragraph separators; retain optional fourth field and original sequence.

records.definition: Paragraph separator in distributed TSV.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Structural processing marker; neither a negative example nor a paragraph-function class. Preserve punctuation and original markers.
records.computable_validation: Validate row types and count, continuation chains and paragraph separators; retain optional fourth field and original sequence.

records.definition: Editorial title in distributed TSV.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Structural processing marker; neither a negative example nor a paragraph-function class. Preserve punctuation and original markers.
records.computable_validation: Validate row types and count, continuation chains and paragraph separators; retain optional fourth field and original sequence.

records.definition: Elementary discourse unit, typically clause/sentence-level.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Text unit, not an editorial function. An EDU can be outside the argument or joined into an ADU.
records.computable_validation: Validate unique XML IDs, nonempty text, and seg endpoints; no semantic function inference.

records.definition: Argumentatively relevant claim grounded in one or more EDUs.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Only the author-endorsed proposition may be assert; opponent voice can be reported or raised for refutation and need not be author belief.
records.computable_validation: Validate ADU role, graph incidence, grounding paths and referenced IDs; resolve endorsement and paragraph context manually.

records.definition: Combines adjacent EDUs argumentatively relevant only together.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Grouping is not an independent claim or communicative function.
records.computable_validation: Verify joint has at least two adjacent EDU sources and a seg path to ADU; use corpus-specific exceptions if detected.

records.definition: Proponent, presenting or defending main claim.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Dialectical role is not author endorsement: opponent may be a hypothetical voice. A proponent premise may report data rather than state the author’s thesis.
records.computable_validation: Validate allowed role on ADU and retain speaker/role provenance; human review resolves attribution.

records.definition: Opponent, challenging proponent arguments.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Dialectical role is not author endorsement: opponent may be a hypothetical voice. A proponent premise may report data rather than state the author’s thesis.
records.computable_validation: Validate allowed role on ADU and retain speaker/role provenance; human review resolves attribution.

records.definition: Author stance in favor of yes/no issue.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Document stance concerns answer to prompt, not ADU role or paragraph function. Do not conflate stance pro with ADU role pro.
records.computable_validation: Validate optional document attribute vocabulary; preserve separately from ADU type.

records.definition: Author stance against yes/no issue.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Document stance concerns answer to prompt, not ADU role or paragraph function. Do not conflate stance pro with ADU role pro.
records.computable_validation: Validate optional document attribute vocabulary; preserve separately from ADU type.

records.definition: Author stance toward the issue is unclear.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Document stance concerns answer to prompt, not ADU role or paragraph function. Do not conflate stance pro with ADU role pro.
records.computable_validation: Validate optional document attribute vocabulary; preserve separately from ADU type.

records.definition: Links EDU to ADU, EDU to joint, or joint to ADU.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: A structural grounding edge is not an argumentation or paragraph function.
records.computable_validation: Validate direction, node types, IDs and continuity; preserve linked or repeated nonadjacent spans.

records.definition: Normal support from source ADU to target ADU.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: The argument relation supports the target, including opponent-to-opponent support; cannot turn all source paragraphs into author-endorsed support.
records.computable_validation: Validate src/trg ADU references and preserve direction; flag role mismatch and review edge meaning and paragraph projection.

records.definition: Support by example from source ADU to target ADU.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Relation encodes argumentative use of example; illustrating intelligibility and supporting a claim are distinct and need paragraph/context review.
records.computable_validation: Validate endpoints and direction; preserve source target and check cross-paragraph placement; semantic adequacy is editorial.

records.definition: Additional source of a relation with more than one premise, including combined/convergent arguments.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Additional premise is graph structure; preserve other premises and original target structure rather than invent a simple independent support edge.
records.computable_validation: Validate references and connected base edge in release representation; inspect actual files before enforcing node/edge endpoint constraints.

records.definition: Rebutting attack on a proposition/ADU.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: An outright refutation is not automatically a limitation or concession; do not reverse polarity into support.
records.computable_validation: Validate ADU references and polarity; an attack has no direct harness relation equivalent; review contextual qualification.

records.definition: Undercutting attack on an inference or relation, not necessarily on the proposition itself.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: An exception may qualify an inference but attack may instead refute it; preserve edge-to-edge target and do not flatten it into a node attack.
records.computable_validation: Validate source ADU and target edge IDs and reject dangling references; semantic distinction and qualification require human review.

records.unit: graph root concept, sometimes inferred implicit segment
records.definition: Core proposition for which the author argues; may be implicit and inserted as MC.
records.necessary_context_or_counterexample: Claim may be an inferred inserted segment with no actual text span; do not fabricate a quote, span or a paragraph function.
records.computable_validation: Verify root in argument subgraph after parsing seg and relation edges, retain inferred status; review centrality and text provenance.
